meta.title: Alice Wright Used as Tactical Email Coercion Agent During Fringe Takeover
meta.source_description: Alice Wright offers 'support' by managing Ben's artists; Fringe uses vulnerable reply to coordinate manipulative PR response

contradictions.summary: Between 6–9 May 2025, Alice Wright positioned herself as a supporter offering 'help' with ticketing and cancellations, but her email was in fact an operational handover pitch that framed the Fringe’s takeover as supportive care. After a vulnerable email from Ben Carter that day, Brighton Fringe responded with a carefully coordinated message containing phrasing Alice had seeded ('we’re so relieved you don’t hate us'). By May 9, Ben confronted the Fringe directly for coercing Alice and exploiting emotional disclosures. This exchange proves Brighton Fringe leveraged Alice’s relationship with Ben to manipulate trust and communication boundaries during a critical safeguarding period.

timeline_entries.summary: Alice Wright begins 'support' narrative in morning email, masking the setup of takeover infrastructure.
Alice Wright offers to handle 'ticketing problems' and show cancellations, implying takeover of Half a Camel's operations.
Ben sends emotional email to Fringe seeking reconciliation and shared goals. Email later used as setup for manipulative reply.
Fringe replies with 'we’re so relieved you don’t hate us' — a phrase Alice admitted planting. Reply weaponised Ben’s vulnerability.
Ben accuses Fringe of coercion and demands reputation restored. Direct quote: 'You coerced Alice into this, you are evil.'
Alice Wright begins infrastructure-level control of Half a Camel’s ticketing and API sync under the guise of support.

Ben sends solicitor-style safeguarding letter documenting suicide risk, emotional distress, and lack of response from Brighton Fringe. Alice confirms she is scripting their reply and downplaying responsibility, saying: 'You didn’t need to apologise but I am encouraging them to tell you they don’t hate you.'

Alice Wright discloses she works for Brighton Fringe on communications, exits personal role, and declares she no longer has a contract with Ben. Ben replies that Duncan is now part of his suicide timeline and must be held accountable. Alice tries to manage this split while maintaining control of messaging.

Brighton Fringe confirms it has been logging all of Ben Carter’s communications, including police reports. Ben asks directly: 'What has Alice told you then?' and discloses venue abuse due to Voodoo's cooperation with his abuser. Fringe does not respond to key safeguarding questions.

Ben Carter sends two emails to Brighton Fringe demanding a public admission of failure after his abuser breached bail. He writes: 'This is my abuser… That is what you want, that is what will be in my case,' and minutes later: 'You coerced Alice into this. You are evil. The things I shared with her — so much pain.'
